# What Tencent Cloud SecretIds the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every SecretId here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef carried on
# through the alphabet, which no real credential is. A body of thirty-two
# characters runs to v; one of sixty-four runs the alphabet out and begins it
# again. The cases about the hyphen and the underscore carry one at the
# positions the case is about and nowhere else, since the run itself spells
# neither. A body of one repeated character is a shape no run can state, and the
# case named "a placeholder written where a value goes" is where that stands.

patterns: tencentcloud-secret-id

# The two shapes Tencent Cloud's published examples show behind the AKID
# prefix: thirty-two characters naming the account or the sub-user a signed call
# is made as, and sixty-four for the SecretId a temporary credential carries.
# Each is stated once rather than being assumed to follow from the other.

case:     a secret id in an environment assignment
in:       TENCENTCLOUD_SECRET_ID=AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv
out:      TENCENTCLOUD_SECRET_ID=«tencentcloud-secret-id»

case:     a temporary secret id
in:       AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqr
out:      «tencentcloud-secret-id»

case:     a secret id in a credentials profile
in:       [default]\nsecret_id = AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv
out:      [default]\nsecret_id = «tencentcloud-secret-id»

case:     a secret id in the json a temporary credential arrives in
in:       {"Credentials":{"TmpSecretId":"AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqr","ExpiredTime":1755388800}}
out:      {"Credentials":{"TmpSecretId":"«tencentcloud-secret-id»","ExpiredTime":1755388800}}

case:     a secret id in the query string of a signed url
in:       https://example.cos.ap-tokyo.myqcloud.com/x?q-ak=AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv&q-sign-time=0
out:      https://example.cos.ap-tokyo.myqcloud.com/x?q-ak=«tencentcloud-secret-id»&q-sign-time=0

case:     a secret id on a command line
in:       tccli configure set secretId AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv
out:      tccli configure set secretId «tencentcloud-secret-id»

# The alphabets, which are what separates the two shapes. The shorter body is
# the letters of both cases and the digits; the longer one is those and the
# hyphen and the underscore besides. So a hyphen among the first thirty-two
# characters rules the shorter shape out, and what is left is the longer one or
# nothing at all.

case:     a hyphen and an underscore in a body of sixty-four characters
in:       AKID0123456789abcdef-123456789abcdef_123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv
out:      «tencentcloud-secret-id»

case:     a hyphen in a body of thirty-two characters
in:       AKID0123456789abcdef-123456789abcdefghij.
out:      AKID0123456789abcdef-123456789abcdefghij.

# The counts, which Tencent Cloud states nowhere in words: both are read off the
# lengths its published examples fall on, and bodies of other lengths are
# published beside them. builtin_tencentcloud_secret_id.go weighs that reading
# and what it rests on. The case named "a body of the length the vendor prints
# as its own field example" is what it costs, written down here so it is not
# something a reader discovers.
#
# They are used as counts and not as floors: thirty-one characters behind the
# prefix are no SecretId, and thirty-six are a SecretId and four characters that
# belong to no credential. The second of those is the price of having no
# boundary behind the match, and a boundary there would drop the SecretId rather
# than trim it.

case:     a body of thirty-two characters is a secret id
in:       AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv
out:      «tencentcloud-secret-id»

case:     a body of thirty-one characters is not
in:       AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstu.
out:      AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstu.

case:     a body of the length the vendor prints as its own field example
in:       SecretId: AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqr
out:      SecretId: AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqr

case:     an alphabet run longer than the shorter shape is a secret id and what follows it
in:       AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz.
out:      «tencentcloud-secret-id»wxyz.

case:     a body one character short of the longer shape is the shorter shape
in:       AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijklmnopq.
out:      «tencentcloud-secret-id»wxyz0123456789abcdefghijklmnopq.

# Two shapes at one prefix, and which of them the scan reads first. The shorter
# body's alphabet is inside the longer one's, so a temporary SecretId carries
# the shorter shape at its own first thirty-six characters whenever neither the
# hyphen nor the underscore stands among them. Reading the shorter
# one first would redact those thirty-six and leave the thirty-two behind them
# in the text, so the longer shape is read first and the whole of the value
# goes.
#
# That order is paid for, and the last case here is what it costs: a SecretId of
# the shorter shape with a run of base64url written against it is the longer
# shape's sixty-four characters behind the prefix, so the run is taken with the
# value. Both halves of the trade are cases so that reversing the order means
# arguing with both.

case:     two secret ids with nothing between them are the longer shape at the first
in:       AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvAKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv
out:      «tencentcloud-secret-id»

case:     the same two with a space between them are one span apiece
in:       AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv
out:      «tencentcloud-secret-id» «tencentcloud-secret-id»

case:     a secret id with a base64url run written against it takes the run with it
in:       AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuveyJzdWIiOiIwMTIzNDU2Nzg5YWJjZGVmIn0
out:      «tencentcloud-secret-id»In0

# What a SecretId may be written against. The prefix is the whole of the anchor
# and there is no boundary on either side of it, so a SecretId keeps its span
# whatever word character it abuts.

case:     a secret id after an underscore
in:       TENCENTCLOUD_SECRET_ID_AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv
out:      TENCENTCLOUD_SECRET_ID_«tencentcloud-secret-id»

case:     a secret id after a letter
in:       xAKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv
out:      x«tencentcloud-secret-id»

case:     a secret id beginning inside the one before it
in:       AKIDAKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv
out:      «tencentcloud-secret-id»

case:     a secret id on each of three lines
in:       AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv\nAKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv\nAKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv
out:      «tencentcloud-secret-id»\n«tencentcloud-secret-id»\n«tencentcloud-secret-id»

# Punctuation ends a body, so nothing written after a SecretId joins it.

case:     a secret id before a host name
in:       host=AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv.example.com
out:      host=«tencentcloud-secret-id».example.com

case:     a secret id at the end of a sentence
in:       the secret id is AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv.
out:      the secret id is «tencentcloud-secret-id».

case:     a secret id flush against a multi-byte rune on both sides
in:       日本語AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv日本語
out:      日本語«tencentcloud-secret-id»日本語

case:     a secret id in a markdown code span
in:       `AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv`
out:      `«tencentcloud-secret-id»`

# And what this pattern leaves alone. The prefix is the whole of what opens a
# candidate, so a character of it in the wrong case, or one character of it
# different, ends the reading before any body is looked at — which is what keeps
# the access key ID prefix of another cloud out, since the two differ at their
# last character alone.

case:     a lowercase prefix
in:       akid0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv
out:      akid0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv

case:     a prefix with one letter in the wrong case
in:       AKId0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv
out:      AKId0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv

case:     the access key id prefix of another cloud, which differs at its last character
in:       AKIA0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv
out:      AKIA0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv

case:     an underscore at the last position of the shorter body
in:       AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstu_
out:      AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstu_

case:     a space where the body would be
in:       AKID 123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv
out:      AKID 123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv

case:     a placeholder written where a value goes
in:       secretId: AKIDxxxxxxxxxxxx
out:      secretId: AKIDxxxxxxxxxxxx

case:     thirty-two characters of the alphabet that open with no prefix
in:       0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv
out:      0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv

case:     the prefix written into prose
in:       the akid prefix is what opens one of these
out:      the akid prefix is what opens one of these

case:     prose in capitals
in:       THERE IS NO CREDENTIAL IN THIS SENTENCE
out:      THERE IS NO CREDENTIAL IN THIS SENTENCE

# And the other half of a Tencent Cloud API key, which this pattern does not
# reach. The SecretKey is what signs a request where the SecretId names who
# signed it, and Tencent Cloud publishes no prefix and no length for it, so
# nothing in such a value says what it is and only the name written in front of
# it would. This pattern reads no name: the prefix is the whole of what it looks
# for.

case:     a secret key beside the secret id it belongs to
in:       TENCENTCLOUD_SECRET_ID=AKID0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv\nTENCENTCLOUD_SECRET_KEY=0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv
out:      TENCENTCLOUD_SECRET_ID=«tencentcloud-secret-id»\nTENCENTCLOUD_SECRET_KEY=0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv
